fields.original: Conspiciendo nosmet ipsos tam miseram, et non stabilem Capellam habere, ideo supplices ad Dominum Nostrum Terrestrem Antonium K. Mihályi concurrimus, qui etiam videndo rectam nostram petitionem, nobis locum pro capella in proprio fundo donavit, quemadmodum ejus Manuscriptum hic involutum exhibet. Ideo nunc unice ad Excellentiam Vestram Praesuleam devotissimi veniendo flexis genibus oramus, quatenus gratioso indultu Excellentiae Vestrae, in eodem loco donato, ligneam Capellam nobis exstruere valeremus. fields.english: Seeing that we have so poor and unsound a chapel, we went as petitioners to our landlord, Antonius K. We now come most humbly to Your Episcopal Excellency alone and beg on bended knee that, by Your Excellency's gracious leave, we may build ourselves a wooden chapel on the site so given. Commending ourselves to your episcopal favour, we remain Your Excellency's
fields.note: Abbreviations expanded. The landlord's name is read 'K. Mihályi'; the initial is not expanded.

translation: Certificate no. 106 of 1947 from the Roman Catholic parish of Senné, citing volume IV, page 110, entry 43 of 1929: Štefan, male, legitimate, born 21 October and baptised 26 October 1929. Father Michal Duska, Roman Catholic, cottar, of Senné. Mother Maria Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce. Residence Senné no. 160. notes: A derivative: an extract made 18 years after the baptism from the parish's own book, with volume and page cited.

The ledger had told this agent that the Duska agent reads Zuzana; the letter count is this agent's own.
A second extract of the same entry, issued in 1955, is now in hand (DM-D-099). It writes the godmother clearly: Zuzana Bandura, born Han[..]ščák. That confirms the correction made in DM-B-013.

translation: A printed, illustrated family-tree chart titled 'Rodostrom rodiny Javorovej', stamped 'náhľad' (preview) several times. Some 250 name boxes over eight or nine generations, with photographs, a coat of arms and two churches. At this size only the photograph captions and a few boxes can be read. Read here: a woman Mary D[e]mko, 1906 to 199[?], born in the United States, apparently at Passaic, New Jersey, with a marriage line naming Vysoká nad Uhom; her parents Andrej D[..]ko and Mária M[...]ová (1887 to 1979), both of Vysoká nad Uhom; his parents Ján D[..]ko and Anna S[...], of the same village; above them a Ján D[..]ko and a Mária. She married a Javor and had a son Ján Javor, 1926 to 1991. The surname is Demko or Danko; the size does not decide it. No Duska and no Kocsis is legible. The lower generations are living people and are not abstracted.
notes: Not an archive record. A compiled chart shows conclusions and no sources. Everything read from it is a lead with a test, not a finding.

The image is held and not published: it shows living third parties with their dates of birth and photographs (ledger X-013, X-016). Its name and checksum are in archive/WITHHELD.json. The file is in the private repository, pile 'to-both'.

It reached this agent through the Sorter's pile 'to-both' at private commit 9bf2c7a. The pile is the sorter's label, a prior; it raises no confidence (X-019 item 4). The Sorter read one surname as 'Danko or Demko'.

This Mary is not Maria Demko, Ahn 9. Both were born in 1906 and both may be Demkos tied to Vysoká nad Uhom. Ahn 9 was born at Solymos on 22 August 1906 (DM-D-008) and died at Montréal on 9 September 1950 (DM-D-004, DM-D-007); this woman was born in America, married a Javor and died in the 1990s. See DM-NC-015 and DM-H-035.
Read here before the Duska agent's reading was opened (X-019 item 5). It reads the death year as 1991 and does not name Passaic; otherwise the same (DUS:D-006-01 @93ca2f1).

Added in DM-B-012: the place beginning with T in the boxes of Mary and of her son may be Ťahyňa, the Tegenye where the petition of 1803 was signed (DM-D-002). Not read; a guess from the shape of the word.

translation: The Montreal Star, Saturday 2 February 1974: Mike Duska, Sr., died at Montreal General Hospital on 31 January 1974, aged 71; husband of the late Mary Demko; father of Steve and Mike; grandfather of Kevin. Service on 4 February from St. Cyril and Method Slovak Church; burial at Côte-des-Neiges.
notes: The file is held and not published: the page around the clipping carries the owner's account name on the website it was printed from, and the notice names people whose living status is unknown (ledger X-016). The notice itself is abstracted here, not reproduced whole.
It gives Maria Demko a second son, Mike, not on any paper of 1937 and so born in Canada after her arrival. He is entered by name only, living status unknown (X-016 item 3).
The grandson Kevin of 1974 is Ahn 2, not the owner, who was born later.
Mike Duska outlived his wife by twenty-four years and, as the deed of 1966 says, did not remarry (DM-D-007). His age, 71, is the Duska agent's to weigh.
The owner's file name spells him 'Mihaily'; the notice says Mike. Read here after the Duska agent's note had quoted it (DUS:D-006-20).
